snippet.title: Commodore 64 Longplay (Windham Classics) Swiss Family Robinson
snippet.description:
Swiss Family Robinson is a graphic text adventure for the Commodore 64, developed by Tom Snyder Productions and published under the Windham Classics label in 1984. It is based on Johann David Wyss's classic 1812 novel, placing the player directly into the family's struggle to survive after being shipwrecked on a remote tropical island.

The player takes the role of Fritz, the eldest son. The adventure begins immediately after the shipwreck, with Fritz and his family stranded on rocks near the island. The first objective is to find a way to get everyone safely ashore. Once on land, the family must establish a shelter and secure the necessities required to survive.

Survival is the central theme. The player must find food and water, construct shelter, explore the island and deal with storms, animals and other dangers. Time continues to pass during the game, making survival management important rather than simply exploring at leisure.

The game uses a text parser combined with high-resolution graphics. Players type commands to move, examine their surroundings, communicate with family members and manipulate objects. Helpful features include a mapping system, inventory information, a Help key and a "World Traveler's Guide to Nature", which provides information about plants, animals and survival techniques.

There are a number of distinct goals throughout the adventure, including getting the family ashore, building a tent, obtaining sufficient food for the rainy season and ultimately achieving rescue. The game can also be saved, allowing the lengthy adventure to be continued later.

The C64 version was specifically adapted by Leonard Bertoni and was distributed on floppy disk. It was designed as both an adventure and an educational introduction to survival and classic literature, fitting Windham Classics' objective of bringing well-known books to young computer users.

Swiss Family Robinson is particularly significant as an early example of a literary adventure game designed around survival rather than combat. Its combination of interactive fiction, graphics, mapping, nature information and practical survival problems makes it considerably more ambitious than many straightforward text adventures of the period.

Notable people

Johann David Wyss — Swiss author of The Swiss Family Robinson, the literary source for the game.

Gabrielle Savage — Program author and one of the principal creators of the game.

David A. Dockterman — Scriptwriter and part of the editorial development team.

Thomas F. F. Snyder — Musician and founder of Tom Snyder Productions.

Leonard Bertoni — Programmer responsible for the Commodore 64 and Apple II versions.

Laya Steinberg — Programmer graphics contributor.

Sharon Cohen — Program graphics contributor.

Peter H. Reynolds — Art direction and illustrations.

Karen Whittredge — Editorial development.

Richard D. Abrams — Project manager.

Tom Snyder Productions, Inc. — Developer of the game.

Windham Classics Corporation — Publisher and owner of the Windham Classics adventure-game line.
